onePager.heroTitle: How to build a website with AI
onePager.heroEyebrow: Copy · Content strategy · Websites built with AI
onePager.heroSubtitle: AI writes the code. Decisions stay on the human side.
onePager.heroLead: AI can write a website's code in a few hours. It won't decide what to tell your clients, in what order, or why they should trust you. That's my job: from decisions and copy to a working website.
onePager.heroPrompt: Build me a website for my law firm.
onePager.heroLastLine: // What should convince your client? No data.
onePager.aiRoleTitle: AI is a coding tool. Not a decision-maker.
onePager.aiRoleLead: Building a website has four stages. In the first three, AI can make suggestions, but it doesn't know your market, your clients or what sets you apart. That's why decisions, design and planning stay with people. AI gets the job where it's fastest: the code.

onePager.aboutTitle: You know your field. I know how to explain it.
aboutParagraphs: Think of me as an editor who works on your side.

Specialists rarely lack knowledge. The trouble starts when they have to explain it to someone who doesn't have it: a patient, a law firm's client, someone coming to their first yoga class. The copy ends up too technical or too vague.

My approach is simple. I ask what clients ask you the first time they get in touch, what worries them and why they choose you. Those answers become the copy first and the website second. AI writes the code; I decide what goes on the page.
I don't write copy to fill a website. Every sentence should answer a specific question or remove a specific doubt. If it doesn't, I cut it.
My goal is a website your clients understand on the first read and AI assistants can cite as a source.

faqItems.q: Can you build a website with AI without a developer?
faqItems.a: Yes, as far as the code goes. Tools like Claude Code or Cursor write working code from a description. The hard part is elsewhere: AI needs clear decisions about what the site should do, who it's for and what it should say. Without them, you get a website that works technically but says nothing.

faqItems.q: What does AI help with when building a website, and what doesn't it help with?
faqItems.a: AI helps with the code: components, styles, animations, fixes and tests. It won't replace decisions about who you're talking to, what you promise and how you stand out. It also won't create your site structure or content plan, because it doesn't know your clients.

faqItems.q: Will AI write the copy for my website?
faqItems.a: It will, but the copy will usually sound like your competitors'. AI averages what already exists online. Good copy needs specifics only you have: numbers, procedures, examples, limits. My job is to draw them out in conversation and write them down in plain language.

faqItems.q: How long does it take to build a website with AI?
faqItems.a: A landing page usually takes 1–2 weeks, a company website with a blog 3–6 weeks. Decisions and copy take most of the time, not the code.

faqItems.q: Will I be able to edit the content myself?
faqItems.a: Yes. I build websites on Sanity, which gives you a panel to change text, images and blog posts without touching the code.

faqItems.q: Will a website built with AI show up in Google and ChatGPT?
faqItems.a: The tool used to write the code doesn't matter. What matters is the content and the technical side: clear answers to clients' questions, a correct heading structure, structured data and fast loading. I take care of that at every stage.

By the hour, at the rates shown in the pricing examples. The first conversation is free. Before we start, you get an estimate of the hours. If the scope changes, I tell you before we go over the estimate.

faqItems.q: Do you also write in English?
faqItems.a: Yes. I write and edit copy in Polish and English. I can prepare both versions of your website from scratch or translate and edit the version you already have.
